item: The storage-events journal keeps the longest events as well as the newest: the cap of the gate holds, guard engagements, pool timeouts and store opens is split, the ten (five) longest by duration and the rest the newest, each kept event saying why in picked_by
summary: The 16 Oct 2026 bundles kept the newest 20 gate holds, and the longest of the session (219.6 s) was not among them: a stream of newer, shorter holds had pushed it out, so the journal showed the lead-up to a crash and hid the worst stall of the week. storage_events.LONGEST splits the cap of four kinds: gate_hold keeps its 10 longest by seconds and 10 newest, guard 5 and 5 by seconds, pool_timeout 5 and 5 by waited_s, open 5 and 5 by total_ms; a repeat of both is counted once and the spare room goes to the next newest, so the kept list never exceeds the cap and the totals and dropped counts are unchanged. Ties go to the newer; a bool, a string or a NaN is never a length. Each kept event carries picked_by (longest, newest or both) and each split kind a keep_rule line. The rule applies on record, on reading the file and on combining the file with this process, so an earlier process's longest hold survives a restart; an event that is cut is released from the open table so a late update returns False. The budget cut drops the oldest of the others first and a longest event last. Widest journal 118,424 bytes (ordinary names 73,714) against the slot of 125,000, the rule adding 1,494. 29 tests, 23 mutants each killed by a named test.
